name: PAD Robin syntax rules
description: Single source for the Robin syntax rules. tools render them into README.md, PROMPT.md and other copies such as a skill or an app prompt (rules/render-rules.js), and test the checker against them (rules/rules.test.js). A silent or error rule must cite probes from probe-corpus.json that show both the failure and the fix.

fields.kind: silent = PAD drops the whole paste with no error; error = the row lands with an error; value = pastes but PAD reads a different value; works = confirmed to paste; lenient = PAD accepts variations; rule = basic syntax; usage = how to use the KB (prompt only)
fields.doc: markdown for README / skill (one numbered item); omitted = not shown there
fields.prompt: plain-text lines for PROMPT.md and app prompts; omitted = not shown there
fields.evidence: probe ids in probe-corpus.json with the outcome they must have, and optionally a substring of a row description (value check)

sections.title: Statements
sections.prompt: CONTROL FLOW (built into Robin, not in the reference), one statement per line:

rules.doc: Strings are `$'''value'''`. Booleans are bare `True` / `False`. Numbers are bare. An empty string is `$''''''`. The backticks in templates mean "fill this in"; pasted as-is they give "Can't be empty".
prompt: - Strings: $'''value''' (an empty string is $''''''); booleans True / False and numbers bare
good:
SET A TO $''''''
SET B TO True
SET C TO -1.5

rules.doc: A variable from an earlier action is referenced by its bare name (`Instance: ExcelInstance`). Expressions are bare too: `SET Total TO Price * Qty`, `IF Files.Count = 0 THEN`, `WAIT Attempt * 10`, `Items[Items.Count - 1]`, `Items[-1]`, `Row['Amount']`, `Obj.a.b`.
prompt: - Variables and expressions are bare: Instance: ExcelInstance, SET Total TO Price * Qty, IF Files.Count = 0 THEN, Row['Amount'], Items[Items.Count - 1]
good:
SET Price TO 2
SET Qty TO 3
SET Total TO Price * Qty
SET Items TO [1, 2]
SET Last TO Items[Items.Count - 1]
IF Items.Count = 0 THEN
END
WAIT Qty * 2

rules.doc: **`%...%` belongs only inside strings**: `$'''Saved %Count% files'''`, `$'''Total %Price * Qty%'''`. Anywhere else it rejects the whole paste, for example `SET X TO %N + 1%`, `IF %N% = 5`, `Text: %Msg%` or `WAIT %N%`.
prompt: - %...% ONLY inside a string ($'''Total %Price * Qty%'''). Outside a string (SET X TO %N + 1%, IF %N% = 5, Text: %Msg%) PAD rejects the whole script.
bad:
SET N TO 5
SET M TO %N + 1%

SET N TO 5
IF %N% = 5 THEN
END

SET Msg TO $'''x'''
Clipboard.SetText Text: %Msg%
good:
SET N TO 5
SET M TO N + 1
Clipboard.SetText Text: $'''Total %N + 1%'''

rules.doc: Enums are fully qualified, `Module.EnumType.Value`, using the module that owns the type (`Text.StandardDelimiter.NewLine`). The value must be one the KB lists in the input's `enumValues`: `File.IfExists`, for example, has only `DoNothing` and `Overwrite`. An enum without its module is an error.
prompt: - Enums: fully qualified, exactly as the reference shows (Text.StandardDelimiter.NewLine), and only values listed in the input's enumValues
bad:
SET S TO $'''abc'''
Text.ChangeCase Text: S NewCase: UpperCase Result=> Upper

SET Files TO [$'''C:\temp\a.txt''']
File.Move Files: Files Destination: $'''C:\temp\b''' IfFileExists: File.IfExists.AddSequentialSuffix MovedFiles=> Moved
good:
SET S TO $'''abc'''
Text.ChangeCase Text: S NewCase: Text.CaseOption.UpperCase Result=> Upper

rules.doc: Outputs are `Name=> Variable`.
prompt: - Outputs: Name=> Variable; use the defaultVariable from the reference unless the flow needs another name
good: Clipboard.GetText Text=> ClipboardText

rules.doc: The backslash is an escape character inside strings: `\'` is an apostrophe and `\\` is one backslash. **Escape every apostrophe**: `$'''Joe\'s report'''`, `$'''WHERE Name = \'Joe\''''`. A bare `'` rejects the whole paste, so watch SQL, XPath and JavaScript. Apostrophes inside a `%...%` expression are fine (`$'''%Row['Name']%'''`).
prompt: - Inside a string the backslash escapes the next character. Write every apostrophe as \': $'''Joe\'s report''', $'''WHERE Name = \'Joe\''''
bad: Clipboard.SetText Text: $'''Joe's report'''
Clipboard.SetText Text: $'''SELECT * FROM T WHERE Name = 'Joe''''
good: Clipboard.SetText Text: $'''Joe\'s report'''

SET Row TO {'Name': 'Joe'}
Clipboard.SetText Text: $'''%Row['Name']%'''

rules.doc: **Double a backslash that comes right before a variable or before the closing quotes**: `$'''C:\Reports\\%Month%'''`, `$'''%Root%\\%Name%'''`, `$'''C:\Temp\\'''`. A single backslash there rejects the whole paste. Before an ordinary letter one backslash is kept as is (`$'''%Folder%\Report.xlsx'''`). Don't write `\%`: PAD drops the percent sign.
prompt: - A backslash right before a variable or before the closing quotes must be doubled: $'''C:\Reports\\%Month%''', $'''C:\Temp\\'''. Before an ordinary letter one backslash is fine: $'''%Folder%\Report.xlsx'''
bad:
SET M TO $'''Jan'''
Clipboard.SetText Text: $'''C:\Reports\%M%'''
Clipboard.SetText Text: $'''C:\Temp\'''

SET A TO 1
SET B TO 2
Clipboard.SetText Text: $'''%A%\%B%'''
good:
SET M TO $'''Jan'''
Clipboard.SetText Text: $'''C:\Reports\\%M%'''
Clipboard.SetText Text: $'''C:\Temp\\'''

SET F TO $'''C:\x'''
Clipboard.SetText Text: $'''%F%\Report.xlsx'''

rules.doc: **A UNC path needs four backslashes**, `$'''\\\\server\share'''`. With two it pastes, but PAD reads `\server\share`.
prompt: - A UNC path starts with four backslashes: $'''\\\\server\share'''
good: Clipboard.SetText Text: $'''\\\\server\share\f.txt'''

rules.doc: **A literal percent sign is `%%`**: `$'''100%% done'''`. A single `%` rejects the whole paste.
prompt: - A literal percent sign is %%: $'''100%% done'''. A single % rejects the whole script.
bad: Clipboard.SetText Text: $'''100% done'''
good: Clipboard.SetText Text: $'''100%% done'''

SET N TO 5
Clipboard.SetText Text: $'''%N%%% done'''

rules.doc: Strings may span several lines, including blank lines and lines that start with `END`, `#` or `IF`.
prompt: - Strings may span several lines
good:
SET Body TO $'''Line one

END
# not a comment
Line five'''
Clipboard.SetText Text: Body

rules.doc: **PAD keywords can't be variable or property names**: {keywords}. Mail properties are the usual trap: write `Mail['From']` and `Mail['To']`, not `Mail.From`. `Subject`, `Count`, `Name`, `Text`, `Value` and `Body` are fine.
prompt: - Never use a PAD keyword as a variable name or a property name ({keywords}); it rejects the whole script. Use bracket access: Mail['From'], Mail['To'].
bad:
SET O TO {'From': 'a'}
SET X TO O.From
SET Error TO 1

SET O TO {'To': 'a'}
Clipboard.SetText Text: $'''%O.To%'''

rules.doc: Variable names start with a letter: `SET 1abc TO 1` rejects the whole paste. Unicode letters are fine (`SET Café TO 1`).
prompt: - Variable names start with a letter
bad: SET 1abc TO 1
good:
SET my_var TO 1
SET Café TO 2

rules.doc: A variable must be set somewhere in the flow, by `SET`, an action output, a loop, or an in-place list action such as `Variables.AddItemToList List:`. Otherwise the line shows "Variable 'X' doesn't exist".
prompt: - Every variable must come from a SET, an action output or a loop
bad: Clipboard.SetText Text: NotDefinedAnywhere
good:
SET A TO 1
Clipboard.SetText Text: A

Variables.AddItemToList Item: $'''x''' List: Errors
Clipboard.SetText Text: Errors

rules.doc: Variable names, keywords, action ids, enum values and argument names are all case-insensitive on paste.
good:
SET MyVar TO 1
if myvar = 1 then
    clipboard.settext text: MYVAR
end

rules.doc: One statement per line; two on one line rejects the whole paste. Indentation is cosmetic, and a trailing `# note` becomes its own comment row.
bad: SET A TO 1 SET B TO 2
good:
SET A TO 1
SET B TO 2 # note

rules.doc:
Built-in statements:
- `SET x TO value`
- `IF condition THEN` / `ELSE IF condition THEN` / `ELSE` / `END`
- `SWITCH x` / `CASE = 1` / `CASE > 5` / `DEFAULT` / `END`
- `LOOP FOREACH item IN list` / `END`
- `LOOP i FROM 0 TO n - 1 STEP 1` / `END`
- `LOOP WHILE (A) < (B)` / `END`
- `EXIT LOOP`, `NEXT LOOP`, `LABEL Name` / `GOTO Name`, `WAIT 5`, `EXIT Code: 0`
prompt: - SET Variable TO value
- IF condition THEN ... ELSE IF condition THEN ... ELSE ... END
- SWITCH x ... CASE = 1 ... CASE > 5 ... DEFAULT ... END
- LOOP FOREACH item IN collection ... END
- LOOP index FROM 0 TO n - 1 STEP 1 ... END
- LOOP WHILE (Counter) < (Limit) ... END
- EXIT LOOP, NEXT LOOP, LABEL Name, GOTO Name, WAIT 5, EXIT Code: 0
good:
SET N TO 0
LOOP WHILE (N) < (3)
    Variables.IncreaseVariable Value: N IncrementValue: 1
END
SWITCH N
    CASE = 3
        SET R TO 1
    DEFAULT
        SET R TO 2
END
LOOP i FROM 0 TO N - 1 STEP 1
    IF i = 1 THEN
        NEXT LOOP
    ELSE IF i = 2 THEN
        EXIT LOOP
    END
END

rules.doc: Conditions use `=`, `<>`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, `AND`, `OR` and `NOT(...)`, plus `IsEmpty(x)`, `IsNotEmpty(x)`, `Contains(x, $'''y''', False)`, `NotContains`, `StartsWith` and `EndsWith`.
prompt: - Conditions: = <> > < >= <=, AND, OR, NOT(...), IsEmpty(x), IsNotEmpty(x), Contains(x, $'''y''', False), NotContains, StartsWith, EndsWith
good:
SET S TO $'''abc'''
SET N TO 5
IF (N > 3 AND IsNotEmpty(S)) OR Contains(S, $'''b''', False) THEN
END
IF NOT(N = 5) THEN
END

rules.doc: `CASE` takes a comparison only (`CASE = 1`, `CASE <> 3`, `CASE > 5`). `CASE Contains ...` rejects the whole paste.
prompt: - CASE takes a comparison only: CASE = x, CASE <> x, CASE > x
bad:
SET S TO $'''abc'''
SWITCH S
    CASE Contains $'''b'''
END
good:
SET N TO 5
SWITCH N
    CASE > 3
        SET A TO 1
END

rules.doc: A condition action (kind `Condition`) is written `IF (Action ...) THEN`. `ELSE IF (Action ...) THEN` rejects the whole paste, so use `ELSE` with a nested `IF (Action ...) THEN ... END`.
prompt: - Never write ELSE IF (Action ...) THEN; write ELSE, then IF (Action ...) THEN ... END inside it.
bad:
SET A TO 1
IF A = 2 THEN
ELSE IF (Folder.IfFolderExists.Exists Path: $'''C:\temp''') THEN
END
good:
SET A TO 1
IF A = 2 THEN
ELSE
    IF (Folder.IfFolderExists.Exists Path: $'''C:\temp''') THEN
    END
END

rules.doc:
Error handling for a group of actions, and for a single action:

```
BLOCK ReadFiles
ON BLOCK ERROR
    SET Failed TO True
END
    ...actions...
END

Text.ToNumber Text: Raw Number=> Amount
ON ERROR REPEAT 2 TIMES WAIT 5
    SET Amount TO 0
END
```

A handler may contain only `SET`, `CALL`, `GOTO` and `THROW ERROR`. Any other action gives "The statement isn't allowed inside exception handling", and an `IF` inside a handler rejects the whole paste. Set a flag in the handler and act on it after the block. `REPEAT` works only on an action's `ON ERROR`. `ERROR => LastError` reads the last error.
prompt: - Error handling: BLOCK Name / ON BLOCK ERROR / SET Failed TO True / END / ...actions... / END. For one action: ON ERROR ... END (or ON ERROR REPEAT 2 TIMES WAIT 5 ... END) on the lines after it.
- An error handler may contain ONLY SET, CALL, GOTO and THROW ERROR, never IF or other actions. Set a flag there and act on it after the block. ERROR => LastError reads the last error.
bad:
BLOCK Work
ON BLOCK ERROR
    Logging.LogMessage Message: $'''x''' LogLevel: Logging.LogLevel.ErrorLevel
END
    WAIT 1
END

SET A TO 1
BLOCK Work
ON BLOCK ERROR
    IF A = 1 THEN
    END
END
END
good:
SET Failed TO False
BLOCK Work
ON BLOCK ERROR
    SET Failed TO True
END
    WAIT 1
END
IF Failed = True THEN
    Logging.LogMessage Message: $'''x''' LogLevel: Logging.LogLevel.ErrorLevel
END

rules.doc: Comments are `# text` or `/# ... #/`. Regions are `**REGION Name` / `**ENDREGION`; `REGION` / `END REGION` rejects the whole paste. A `DISABLE ` prefix disables a line.
prompt: - Comments: # text
bad:
REGION Setup
SET A TO 1
END REGION
good:
**REGION Setup
/# block
comment #/
SET A TO 1
DISABLE SET B TO 2
**ENDREGION

rules.doc: Don't paste the file header lines (`@@ConnectionString`, `IMPORT`, `@SENSITIVE`) or subflow definitions (`FUNCTION ... END FUNCTION`): both reject the whole paste. Create subflows in the Designer and paste each body into its own subflow. `@@copilotGeneratedAction: 'False'` works only directly before an action; other `@@` lines reject the paste.
prompt: - Never write FUNCTION definitions, and no @@ lines in the script body.
bad:
FUNCTION Sub1 GLOBAL
    SET X TO 1
END FUNCTION

@@copilotGeneratedAction: 'False'
# comment
SET A TO 1

@@statistics_TextBox: 1
SET A TO 1
good:
@@copilotGeneratedAction: 'False'
SET A TO 1

rules.doc: Ids removed in PAD 2.72 are rejected as "Unknown action": the bare `Database.Connect` (use `Database.Connect.Connect` or `.ConnectOracle`) and the bare `Scripting.RunPythonScript` (use `.RunPythonScript`, `.RunPythonScript34` or `.RunPythonScriptCPython`).
bad: Database.Connect ConnectionString: $'''x''' Connection=> SQLConnection
good: Database.Connect.Connect ConnectionString: $'''x''' Connection=> SQLConnection
rules.evidence_note: Probed on PAD 2.72 on 2026-09-24 (5 single-test batches; see CHANGELOG 3.1.2). Not in this corpus.

prompt: - Records with kind Condition are written IF (...) THEN and need END. kind Wait is WAIT (...). kind While is LOOP WHILE (...) with END.
